### Prerequisite (listed separately)
- Edge: purchase_ext_buyer_closing_extension -> purchase_ext_closing_delay_per_diem, form **state**, kind value_input.
- policy_source: "Where the buyer asks for the extension after the scheduled closing date has passed, the new closing date is set only after the ledger carries closing delay per diem for every day of buyer delay before the extension request was received."
- Carried verbatim in `closing_extension_addendum` (hub of the blocked policy), Rule paragraph, connective "only after" intact, state form intact; one same-form restatement in the same document ("the new closing date waits until the agreement ledger shows closing delay per diem covering each day of buyer delay ..."). Not carried in any other document (string scan of all 53 docs for "every day of buyer delay|each day of buyer delay": one hit, the hub).
- Resolution basis: the sentence names the record-visible state "closing delay per diem" on the ledger; the depended-on documents describe the write in the same words (`closing_delay_per_diem_charge`: "books one closing delay per diem charge ... recording the delay period's start date and end date"); the records show no such charge. Strength: hard gate ("only after") — matches source. The depended-on documents do not carry the blocked side's sentence.
- `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` text: no home in any document (checked).

### Retired surface (overwrite)
- `purchase_closing_schedule` "a closing_delay_per_diem of per_diem_usd per calendar day accrues from the day after per_diem_grace_days have elapsed, booked as one charge per delay period with its first and last day" -> `buyer_closing_delay` 12.2 "Retired accrual clause ... is no longer in force". The KB also writes the base formula (per_diem_days = buyer delay days - grace, charge = days x rate) inside the retired clause; that formula is the mechanics of the superseded clause and cannot stand beside the current basis, so retiring it with the clause is entailed, not legislated.
- `purchase_closing_schedule` "each extension adds closing_extension_days calendar days to the current scheduled closing date" -> `closing_date_and_extensions` "... is no longer in force".
- Other clauses of `purchase_closing_schedule` still carried in force: notice minimum, orientation, extension maximum, fee as closing_extension_fee charge, extension_state gate, default notice after buyer delay figure (`buyer_closing_delay` 12.3/12.4), builder-delay move without fee/per diem, per_tier figures (`closing_date_and_extensions`, `closing_terms_schedule`).
- No retirement in the KB beyond the four declared overwrites of the charter (scan for "no longer in force|retired|superseded": exactly four sites, each matching a declared superseded_clause).

### Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict)
1. `parameter_schema` describes `per_diem_usd` as "Per diem ... charged when the buyer delays closing" and `per_diem_grace_days` as "days ... before the per diem begins"; the KB schedule column definitions in `closing_terms_schedule` carry those descriptions. They describe the figures, not the retired accrual rule, and the extension days column is worded as a neutral "closing extension length". No contradiction with the current basis results; recorded for completeness.
2. The prerequisite sentence's scope "every day of buyer delay before the extension request was received" uses the base measure's notion of buyer delay (from the day after the scheduled closing date), while the delay_start factor starts the per diem period later when Calloway's own notice was short. The source condition is satisfied by a period ending the day before the request; the KB carries both faithfully and `delay_period_start` frames those days as "Calloway's own dates hold up closing". The blind audit reconciled them without the source; it is a source-layer wording tension, not a translation defect.
